observations: Photo 0 is a collage showing three distinct styles of salon chairs.
Top section shows two identical black chairs with square chrome bases and integrated footrests.
Bottom left section shows a black chair with a round chrome base and a taller backrest.
Bottom right section shows a black chair with a round chrome base and curved, open-sided armrests.
All chairs appear to have hydraulic lift levers.
The upholstery is black, likely synthetic leather or PVC.
The chairs are photographed outdoors on a paved surface.
A watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI MAKUO IGBOKWE' is present across the center.

claims.claim: We deal in different salon chairs
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows at least three different models of salon chairs.
The origin of second-hand goods cannot be determined from visual inspection of the exterior.

risks.risk: Hydraulic pump may be seized or leaking fluid.
risks.proof: A video showing the chair being pumped to full height and then released/lowered smoothly.
risks.if_unproven: as having a non-functional hydraulic lift.

risks.risk: The swivel mechanism may be stiff or grinding.
risks.proof: A video showing the chair rotating a full 360 degrees without resistance.
risks.if_unproven: as having a damaged swivel base.

risks.risk: Hidden tears or thinning in the upholstery, especially at the seams.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the seat cushions and armrest edges.

proof_requests: Video of the hydraulic pump lifting and lowering the chair with weight on it.
Video of the chair swiveling 360 degrees.
Close-up photos of the seat and armrest upholstery to check for wear.
Photo of the underside of the base to check for rust or weld repairs.
response.reason: The items are clearly identifiable as salon chairs. While multiple models are shown, they can be priced as generic salon chairs at a base 'worst-case' functional level until mechanical proof is provided.
